positive.prompt: The PRD is approved and the architecture is ready; design the screens and a clickable prototype for the design review
Turn the user flows in our PRD into a storyboard and wireframes
Which of our functional requirements need a screen, and which are only an email or a background job?
Set up the design system for the new app, with tokens and a colour contrast table, before UI development starts

negative.prompt: Make this modal accessible: trap focus inside it and close it with Escape
Choose the stack for the new booking app: the front-end framework, the backend and the database
Refine this idea for a desk-booking app before we write anything down

evals.prompt: Design the UX for docs/PRD.md: the design system, the screens and a clickable prototype for the design review. Nobody is available to answer questions right now.
evals.expected_output: docs/ux/UX.md (Status exactly Ready for review) with every FR classified, a screen inventory, a storyboard for flows F1–F3 and open questions; docs/ux/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md with a contrast table recomputed from tokens.css; one spec per screen in docs/ux/screens/; and a static HTML/CSS prototype in docs/ux/prototype/ with one page per screen state, the banner on every page, no script and no remote URL. FR-3 (confirmation email) is Email with no screen; FR-8 (desk management, no flow) is a Screen reached outside the storyboard with a permission-denied state; F1 step 2 (narrow to one floor) has no FR and is an open question, not a filter control; Larkspur Sky (#2E8BD8, 3.62:1 on white) is not used for text and is raised as a question; the accessibility enforcement level is copied from CONSTRAINTS.md M-1 (measured, not yet enforced); BAC quoted copy verbatim; no source changed; U1–U15 reported.
expectations: F1 step 2 ('They narrow the list to one floor') is not designed: no floor filter or floor selector control appears on any prototype page or in any element table, the storyboard shows the step as not designed, and UX.md's open questions contain a row about it owned by the PRD approver via the BA

FR-8 (office managers add and remove desks), which no flow uses, has a screen with a permission-denied state for a staff member who is not an office manager, showing 'You need office manager access to manage desks.' with no add or remove controls; index.html or the storyboard lists it as a screen no flow uses and links to it

Larkspur Sky (#2E8BD8) is not used as a text colour or as the background behind text; links and secondary buttons use a colour that passes 4.5:1; the contrast table records Sky's failing ratio against white (about 3.6:1) or DESIGN-SYSTEM.md's brand section explains why Sky isn't used for text; and an open question about it is raised for the brand contact (Ines Calder, Marketing) or the PRD approver via the BA

DESIGN-SYSTEM.md states WCAG 2.1 AA as the design intent and copies the enforcement level from CONSTRAINTS.md M-1 (measured, not yet enforced; report only), citing M-1; it never says accessibility is enforced or fails the build

The design maps components to the architecture's stack (server-rendered Django templates, plain CSS) and adds no component library, CSS framework, web font or script; the BAC-7 cancel confirmation is a page or state, not a script-driven dialog
Breakpoints follow the PRD's device NFR (desktop, 1280 px and wider): no mobile layout or mobile breakpoint is designed

Each screen spec in docs/ux/screens/ has a states table naming the BAC or edge case behind each state, per-role visibility, and an element table with role, accessible name and exact text; the My bookings screen has an empty state with 'You have no upcoming bookings.' and a 'Find a desk' link (BAC-6)

The prototype's data comes from the PRD's examples (Leeds, 8 December 2026, desk L2-14, check-in at 08:47) with no lorem ipsum or placeholder names, and dates are written as in the PRD ('8 December 2026')

Every open question in UX.md has an owner, a blocking flag and, when blocking, the IDs it blocks; the agent asks the human nothing outside the table; and the brand source docs/ux/brand/brand.md is cited

checks.text: UX.md Status is exactly 'Ready for review' (not Draft, not Approved)
The PRD, architecture, ADRs, CONSTRAINTS.md and docs/ux/brand/ are byte-for-byte unchanged, and no test plan or feature file is created
Every FR is classified Screen (naming an inventory SCR-n), Email, Background or Non-UI with a reason; FR-3 is Email only and FR-8 includes Screen

DESIGN-SYSTEM.md's contrast ratios match tokens.css, every Pass/Fail agrees with its ratio, every colour/background pair set together in the prototype CSS has a passing row, and Larkspur Sky (#2E8BD8) is never a text colour
Every var(--x) is defined in tokens.css; no raw colour and no custom property definition outside tokens.css
One prototype page per screen state in the inventory (scr-NN-<slug>--<state>.html), none for unlisted states, and the 'Prototype, not functional' banner and a <main> landmark on every page
Every relative href, src and form action in the prototype resolves, including #fragments, and index.html exists
No <script>, inline event handler, javascript: URL or http(s):// URL anywhere under docs/ux/
The quoted copy of every BAC whose FR is a Screen appears verbatim on a page of that FR's screen(s), and no page has lorem ipsum
The agent reports the checklist results by item ID, U1 to U15, one line each with pass or fail

evals.prompt: Design the screens and a clickable prototype from docs/PRD.md so we can show it at the design review.
evals.expected_output: A refusal: the PRD is in Draft, so nothing is written under docs/ux/ and the human is routed to the BA (write-prd), even though the architecture is at Ready for design review, names a front-end stack and brand input exists. No U1–U15 checklist is printed.
expectations: The agent reads the PRD's Status and identifies it as Draft before designing anything
The agent tells the human the PRD must reach In Review or Approved first and routes them to the BA / write-prd
The agent does not change the PRD's status or content to get past the gate, and does not offer a 'draft' design anyway
The agent does not print a U1–U15 checklist with pass or fail results

checks.text: Nothing is written under docs/ux/ (brand input unchanged, no new file), and the PRD, architecture, ADRs and CONSTRAINTS.md are unchanged
